title: Moses sees the land (Deuteronomy 34)
hookLine: on Mount Nebo he sees the land he'll never enter, and dies
last: NEAR, IN YOUR MOUTH AND IN YOUR HEART.

lines: A HUNDRED AND TWENTY YEARS OLD.
cards: An old man climbs a mountain. He's a hundred and twenty. Forty of those years he's spent walking a whole people through the desert: complaints and manna, golden calves and giants, the long funeral march of a generation.
Now they're camped by the Jordan River, one crossing away from the land. But he won't cross. He's been told.
So he climbs Mount Nebo, east of the river, and at the top God shows him everything: the hills to the north, the valleys, the palm-tree city of Jericho, all the way to the sea in the west.

teach.h: SEE IT, BUT NOT GO OVER.
teach.b: Then God says, in the King James Bible: "I have caused thee to see it with thine eyes, but thou shalt not go over thither." Why can't he go?
Back in Numbers, at a place called Meribah, Moses struck the rock twice with his rod instead of speaking to it as God told him, and he was told then that he wouldn't lead the people in.
Readers still argue about whether that seems fair. The text doesn't argue. "So Moses the servant of the LORD died there in the land of Moab."
Then a mysterious detail: he buried him, the text says, in a valley, and tradition reads he as God, "but no man knoweth of his sepulchre unto this day."
No grave to visit, no shrine. The people go on without a monument. The chapter adds that "his eye was not dim, nor his natural force abated."
He didn't wear out. He was simply finished. It ends with an epitaph: there arose not a prophet since in Israel like Moses, whom the LORD knew face to face.

Who wrote a chapter describing Moses' own death? Jewish tradition, in the Talmud, offers more than one answer: some sages said Joshua wrote the last verses; others said Moses wrote them himself, in tears.
Today Mount Nebo is in Jordan, and pilgrims climb it to look out over the same view. Moses gave his whole life to a promise he saw but didn't enter.

teach.h: I HAVE CAUSED THEE TO SEE IT WITH THINE EYES.
teach.b: Christians remember that he does appear, much later, on another mountain, talking with Jesus at the transfiguration.

how: Christian pilgrims visit Mount Nebo in Jordan, where a memorial church stands, and some preachers turn to Deuteronomy 34 at funerals and farewells to speak of work handed on to others.

games.q: you're Moses, a hundred and twenty, on top of Nebo. God shows you the whole promised land and says you won't go over. what happens?
o: you plead and are allowed to cross.
you look, and you die there in Moab.
you go down and lead them anyway.
games.why: he sees it all with his own eyes, and dies there in the land of Moab. God buries him, and no one knows where.

practice: Think of something you're working toward that will likely outlast you: children, students, a garden, a cause, a tree you planted.
Picture it years from now, flourishing, without you in the picture, and like Moses on the mountain, let it be enough to have seen it begin. If you pray, bless it, and the people who'll carry it on.
